answer: I found two forms that were retired in 2026. Both changes took effect on February 1, 2026. The power of attorney form NW-POA-1, which needed a notary, was replaced by NW-POA-2, which can be signed electronically with no notary. In Georgia, a power of attorney still has to be notarized, including NW-POA-2. An NW-POA-1 signed before February 1, 2026 was accepted only until June 30, 2026, so it is no longer accepted. The odometer disclosure statement NW-ODO-1 was replaced by NW-ODO-2. One thing to watch: the older article "Broken or replaced odometer" still tells sellers to use NW-ODO-1, even though that form has been replaced. If there were other retired forms, the help center doesn't list them, so check with a store.
